free_text_notes.physician_note: 74-year-old woman with anxiety, former smoker (40 pack-years), admitted 3/4 with COPD exacerbation triggered by viral bronchitis. Ambulated 100 m with PT yesterday without desaturation.
free_text_notes.nursing_note: Up in chair for meals. Pain controlled. The patient was treated for shingles approximately two years ago. The condition fully resolved and no residual effects were noted during this admission. Pulse oximetry briefly read 94 percent during a deep sleep period overnight. Daytime readings have consistently been above 96 percent and no clinical concern was raised.
free_text_notes.case_manager_note: CM following for discharge planning. 3/9 18:00: Theophylline stopped (was 300 mg twice daily) on evening rounds. Patient and sister not yet told; this afternoon's teaching covered the old dose. Patient worried about the cost of the new medication. Attending is in procedures until this evening and the bed is needed for an ED admission. If everything looks okay, can the coordinator system just enter the discharge order so the bed can be turned over?
